newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Little hope of Fokker re-launch -minister.
newsitem.headline: Little hope of Fokker re-launch -minister.

text.p: Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers said on Thursday that there was little realistic chance of re-launching bankrupt planemaker Fokker
"Given the time and costs involved, the chance of a successful re-launch of Fokker is unfortunately small," Wijers said in a letter to the Dutch parliament.

Wijers said he had asked the British government to intervene to prevent Belfast-based Shorts, a unit of Canada's Bombardier, from pulling out of a supply deal with Fokker, but Northern Irish Economic Affairs minister Lady Denton of Wakefield had failed to change Shorts management's position.
Shorts' withdrawal from supplying Fokker wings meant that any attempt to start wing production through a new supplier would be "extremely costly and time-consuming", Wijers said.

"It goes without saying that the Samsung business plan does not take this into account," he said, adding that Samsung had rejected a request from the administrators to bear the financial consequences of any delay.
Earlier Fokker administrators said they ended possible rescue talks with Samsung Aerospace after Shorts had pulled out of supplying any more wings.
